messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx and TCP resets observed for inference endpoints in az1a starting 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z. Symptoms include DNS timeouts, retransmits, and NLB target flaps. Pager triggered to #incidents.

sre-oncall: Ack. Investigating. Host net errors on multiple g5 instances in az1a. Kicking off tcpdump and health checks.

eng-nw: Pls add: AWS control panel shows noisy network plane for az1a (packet loss spikes). No declared AZ outage but fabric looks degraded.

prod-lead: Any idea on customer impact size? Are SLAs being breached?

support: Snapshot (last 10m): ~80-100 failing inference responses/min, affecting ~12 API keys. Mostly streaming/chat endpoints timing out around 8-12s. No data corruption reports.

ryan: @sre-oncall paste tcpdump snippet so we can see directionality (NLB->instance vs instance->egress).

sre-oncall: here's a short dump (trimmed):
```
12:03:22.345 IP 10.0.1.45.443 > 10.0.2.12.51234: Flags [S.], seq 0, win 65535, length 0
12:03:22.347 IP 10.0.1.45.443 > 10.0.2.12.51234: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0
12:03:27.987 IP 10.0.2.12 > 8.8.8.8: UDP, length 60 (DNS)
12:03:33.102 IP 10.0.2.12 > 8.8.8.8: UDP, length 60 (DNS) (retransmit)
```
Resets on SYNs and DNS retransmits visible.

eng-nw: Also seeing higher latency to NAT and resolver clusters from az1a subnets. Hypothesis: egress path oscillation on some switches/ENIs. Recommend short-term steering of new inference traffic to eu1b.

eng-platform: eu1b Dedicated pool has spare capacity. We can accept a fast-redirect of up to ~40% immediately, with warm-up to 70% over 20 minutes. Model variant match confirmed (v3.2-q4).

sre-oncall: Proposed mitigation:
1) Control-plane route override prefer eu1b for inference.default.
2) Gradual drain/weight reduction of az1a hosts (small batches).
3) Change host resolver to internal VPC resolver to reduce external egress for DNS.
4) Open AWS case with pcap/NLB logs.

maya: CLI to set routing preference: 
```
redwoodctl route update --route inference.default --set-preference region:eu1b --grace 30s
```
If we agree I'll run a 5% canary.

support: Prep customer comms: "We observed elevated error rates in a single AZ and are rerouting traffic to maintain availability. We're monitoring and will update in 15 minutes." Ready to post after mitigation begins.

ryan: Execute canary. @maya run and @sre-oncall start draining a tiny batch. Monitor 60-90s.

maya: Applied canary 5% -> eu1b. Policy rp-az1a-2026-03-15-01 created. CLI returned OK.

incident-bot: ACTION: policy rp-az1a-2026-03-15-01 applied. Canary 5% routing to eu1b.

sre-oncall: Canary slice looks clean for 2m. No visible additional errors. Promoting to 30%.

incident-bot: ACTION: canary promoted to 30% -> eu1b.

eng-nw: Still seeing DNS timeouts from some az1a hosts to external resolvers. Recommend switching those hosts to VPC DNS (169.254.169.253 style internal resolver) to avoid NAT egress hits.

sre-oncall: Initiated resolver change on one host (10.0.2.12) via cloud-init override; monitoring impact before wider rollout.

prod-lead: Do we need AWS engaged?

eng-nw: Case opened with AWS (CASE-84462) with pcaps and NLB logs. They suspect NIC offload or host-level device issues on a small subset.

sre-oncall: After 30% promotion overall 5xx reduced ~60-70%. Some long-tail traffic still hits degraded nodes; continuing drain.

maya: Promoting to 60% now. Warming model cache in eu1b to avoid cold-start latency.

incident-bot: ACTION: promotion to 60% completed.

ryan: Good. Keep draining remaining az1a hosts in 10% batches, sequentially. Keep AWS case updated. Prepare a handoff summary for the next oncall in ~40m.

sre-oncall: Handoff summary draft: suspected network plane impairment in az1a causing NAT/resolver timeouts and TCP RSTs. Mitigations: routing override to eu1b (rp-az1a-2026-03-15-01), draining az1a hosts, local resolver override, AWS case opened. Current: 60% traffic -> eu1b, error rate down ~65%, continuing staged drains. No data loss. Monitoring.

maya: Saving policy and diffs to /incidents/3123456789. Reversion criteria: 30m of stable error metrics and green target health.

support: Posting update to status page and support queue every 15m. No major customer escalations yet.

eng-nw: AWS recommends instance NIC reset/eviction for worst nodes; we'll do sequential graceful evicts, avoiding mass.

sre-oncall: Starting graceful evict on two worst hosts now; watching telemetry.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager suppression active for this incident; critical alerts still propagate.

ryan: Preparing handoff notes and tagging @maya to lead overnight watch. Handoff in 40m. Great job. :thumbsup: 

maya: Taking handoff at 10:00Z. I'll coordinate with AWS on evictions and rollback when safe.

sre-oncall: Pre-handoff check: error-rate steady at 1.9% (baseline 0.5%), evictions for two bad hosts completed, canary traces show healthy responses. Handoff time set.

support: Posting another update: routing to eu1b in effect; ETA for full restore TBD pending AWS confirmation.

eng-nw: Continuing to add ENI/instance counters to the AWS case.

maya: Handoff accepted. Will draft a postmortem when stabilization is complete. If regression occurs ping #incidents immediately.

sre-oncall: Closing active pager loop; monitoring continues. Final snapshot before handoff: error-rate 1.9% (baseline 0.5%), traffic 60% -> eu1b, active drains ongoing.
